what_this_is: F-8c — the path by which the 500-row held-out set enters the rebuilt mixture, measured stage by stage with the project's own identity key.

identity_key.source: v2/export_holdout.py (the exporter that wrote the held-out file), whose own comment states it must match gate_v2.prompt_hash_of and the dedupe key

no_new_data: every file read is already on disk; this script downloads nothing

the_chain.reading: the contamination is present in the fenrir download itself and reaches every later stage — including v3's own training file and training mixture; no stage in this project introduced it

the_gate_record.reading: the v2 admission gate never saw fenrir, so the held-out set's exclusion was never established for the source that actually carries it

the_v3_record.reading: the v3 contamination report's zero covers CyberMetric-500 (and SecQA, whose fingerprint file was a failed-download placeholder and was excluded). It covers neither the 500-row held-out set nor the Trendyol corpus it came from

checks.name: the held-out set is the certified 500-row split, and the identity key is the project's own
checks.detail: 500 rows, 500 distinct canonical identities (sha256 of the lowercased, whitespace-normalised prompt, first 16 hex)

checks.name: the identity key agrees with the v2 gate's own prompt_hash_of on the first 100 rows
checks.detail: 100/100 agree; the gate's own function is used, not re-implemented

checks.name: the leak is present in the fenrir bundle as downloaded, before any of this project's own processing
checks.detail: 605 rows of 220426-CyberSec-Dataset_escaped.jsonl already carry a held-out identity — the contamination predates this project

checks.name: the leak survives the v3 cleaning step
checks.detail: 605 rows of the cleaned fenrir file carry a held-out identity

checks.name: the leak reaches v3's own SFT training file
checks.detail: 604 rows of data/v3/sft/fenrir.jsonl carry a held-out identity — v3 was trained on 0.998 of the 500 held-out questions

checks.name: the leak reaches v3's training mixture
checks.detail: 604 rows of data/v3/mixture/mixture-v3-no-trail.jsonl carry a held-out identity

checks.name: the leak reaches the rebuilt corpus
checks.detail: 604 rows of data/v4/corpus-v4-r3.jsonl carry a held-out identity

checks.name: the leak reaches the rebuilt mixture
checks.detail: 604 rows of data/v4/mixture-v4.jsonl carry a held-out identity

checks.name: the leak is confined to the fenrir stream in the mixture
checks.detail: source labels carrying a held-out identity: ['fenrir']

checks.name: the answers that leak are the held-out reference answers themselves
checks.detail: 499 of 604 comparable rows carry the held-out row's own answer CONTENT; 25 of them are byte-identical and the rest differ only in JSON escaping depth

checks.name: the leaked prompts are byte-identical to the held-out prompts, not paraphrases
checks.detail: 604 of 604 leaked rows carry a byte-identical prompt string; the identity match is not an artefact of normalisation

checks.name: the answer relationship is reported as a measured histogram

checks.name: the held-out set's own source corpus was gated and admitted
checks.detail: the Trendyol corpus — the corpus the held-out split was taken from — is candidate 0 and was admitted, with overlap_max 0.0266

checks.detail: CONTAMINATION_REPORT.md names the held-out set: False. It reports 'contaminated rows: 0' against the populations it names (CyberMetric-500, SecQA; SecQA's fingerprint file was a failed-download placeholder and was excluded) — a different population from the 500-row held-out set, so its zero does not contradict this finding
